Directions for Questions 96 to 100:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:
"The preservation of biodiversity is not merely an aesthetic or ecological desideratum, but the bedrock of human
survival and economic resilience. Every ecosystem operates as a complex web of mutual dependencies; the
collapse of even a single keystone species can trigger trophic cascades that unravel whole habitats. Modern
agricultural monocultures, heavily reliant on a tiny genetic base, remain acutely susceptible to unforeseen climatic
stresses and virulent pathogens. Preserving wild cultivars and conserving intact biological biomes provides the
essential genetic reservoirs needed to engineer disease-resistant crops and develop pharmaceutical compounds.
Sustaining natural capital must therefore be treated as an existential imperative rather than a discretionary
expenditure."
questions.questionText: Why is biodiversity preservation considered essential according to the passage?
options: It forms the bedrock of human survival and economic resilience
It is solely an aesthetic hobby for environmentalists
It facilitates the clearing of forested areas for farming
It minimizes the expenditure on industrial chemicals
